recentItems.title: Trump Declares Himself ‘Mr. Veto’ As Democrats Take Control Of House And Senate After Midterm Rout
recentItems.description:
US President Donald Trump has declared himself “Mr. Veto” after Democrats secured control of both the House of Representatives and Senate in the 2026 midterm elections. Trump’s new title signals a potential clash with the incoming Democratic-led Congress, as the President vows to use his veto power against legislation he opposes. But Trump has also said he is willing to work with Democrats and does not want to spend the next two years vetoing everything. With the new Congress set to begin in January 2027, Washington is bracing for a high-stakes power struggle between the White House and Capitol Hill.

recentItems.title: Europe Bomb Alerts: Dozens Of Flights, Broadcasters SKY, RTE And NOVA TV Stare At Deadly Threats
recentItems.description:
In Ireland, a bomb threat prompted the evacuation of the Dublin headquarters of the national broadcaster RTE, and as a result, live broadcasts were swapped out for pre-recorded programs.

After a few hours had passed, staff made their way back into the building, but only once police officers accompanied by sniffer dogs had carried out a search of the surrounding area and confirmed that it was safe.

An Garda Síochána, the national police force of Ireland, has stated that it has been in communication with Irish media organizations regarding the matter, and it confirmed that the threat will be the subject of an investigation.

Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin said the threats to RTE and others just illustrates how relatively simple it can be to cause disruption and to undermine the normal operation of society through unconventional activities of this kind, which are designed to cause fear and anxiety.

He stated that a very significant security operation would be put in place next week, when Dublin is set to host meetings of the European Political Community and of European Union leaders.

In a separate development, the UK-based broadcaster Sky announced that it too had been the recipient of what it described as a security threat.

In a statement reported by Sky News channel, it said — We are working closely with authorities to ensure our people and operations remain secure.
 
Sky News remained on air.

In the meantime, NOVA TV, which is a privately owned broadcasting company based in Bulgaria, reported that it had received an email containing a threat to bomb the station.

According to the broadcaster, the person who sent the message asserted that they were responsible for the threats directed at European air traffic, and NOVA TV stated that it carried out its usual safety procedures, with no disruption occurring to either its television or its radio broadcasts.

recentItems.title: Russia Ukraine War: Kyiv Hit In Massive Overnight Strike On Military, Energy And Transport Targets
recentItems.description:
Russia has claimed responsibility for a massive overnight strike targeting military, energy and transport infrastructure in Kyiv and surrounding regions. Moscow says the attack hit the Northern Bridge, allegedly used to move military equipment, as well as the Meridian plant, which Russia claims manufactures Flamingo cruise missiles. Power plants, electricity substations and industrial facilities in Kyiv and Zhytomyr were also reportedly targeted. Russia further claimed a cargo vessel in the Black Sea carrying military equipment and dual-use goods was hit. Here’s the latest on the major Russian strike and its impact on Ukraine’s war infrastructure.

recentItems.title: Trump Makes Hardliner Stephen Miller His Chief Of Staff After Midterms Rout| Susie Wiles Says This
recentItems.description:
No Lessons Learnt? Trump Makes Hardliner Stephen Miller His Chief Of Staff After Midterms Rout

President Donald Trump announced that Stephen Miller would succeed Susie Wiles as White House Chief of Staff, appointing a steadfast and assertive confidant known for his unwavering support of the America First agenda. 

This strategic decision comes as the US President prepares to confront a newly empowered Democratic-controlled Congress in the upcoming year.

Miller, who has been a longstanding member of Trump’s close inner circle, serves as a principal architect of the administration’s stringent immigration policies.

He is among the most enduring aides of Donald Trump, having joined the 2016 presidential campaign — initially considered a long shot — as a speechwriter.

He most recently held the position of White House Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy, managing a wide range of responsibilities; however, he is primarily recognized for his involvement in the formulation and implementation of immigration policy during the Trump administration.

The recent personnel changes indicate that Trump, whose Republican Party suffered significant losses in the midterm elections, is opposing a conciliatory strategy toward Democratic legislators, who are intent on conducting investigations into the administration — Miller himself being a primary focus.

At 41 years of age, Miller is a steadfast advocate for Trump and has developed an extensive and nuanced comprehension of presidential executive authority as well as the functioning of the federal government.

This expertise suggests the likelihood of a significant increase in executive actions during the remaining two years of Trump’s administration.
